title: Prescription Insurance on File Continuation Supply: Definition of the Days Supply
content:
## Definition

Under **Prescription Insurance on File**, the days supply of a continuation supply is the number of calendar days from the claim's date of service to the decision due date of the most recent appeal on the coverage, counting the decision due date and not the date of service. When no appeal is on the coverage, the days to a decision due date are 0.

The continuation days supply is never less than 1 day and, after that, never more than the plan class's largest days supply per claim.

## Terms

- **The continued drug** — the prescription the most recent denial on the coverage concerns.
- **Date of service** — the date of the continuation claim.
- **Decision due date** — the date recorded on the most recent appeal on the coverage by which the plan must decide.
- **Largest days supply per claim** — the plan class's figure, as the plan-class schedule gives it.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

| Date of service | Most recent appeal's decision due date | Calendar days counted (due date counted, date of service not) | Class's largest days supply (hypothetical) | Continuation days supply |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 June | 17 June | 11 to 17 June: 7 | 34 | 7 |
| 10 June | 10 July | 11 June to 10 July: 30 | 34 | 30 |
| 10 June | 25 July | 11 June to 25 July: 45 | 34 | 34 |
| 10 June | no appeal on the coverage | 0 | 34 | 1 |

In the third row the 45 days are first held to at least 1 day, which they already are, and then to no more than 34 days. In the last row 0 days are raised to 1 day.
